rationale: B first collects every cell that depends on the changed input, directly or indirectly, and then recomputes each one only after all of its inputs have settled. Updates are therefore glitch-free and each cell is computed exactly once, with comments explaining both phases. ComputeCell.value is a read-only property, so outside code cannot overwrite a computed value. A uses a LIFO worklist that can recompute a cell before its inputs are up to date, relying on repeated recomputation to converge. It also leaves ComputeCell.value as a plain writable attribute and reaches into other cells' private _observers from a module-level function. A's 'fire callbacks after comparing with the original values' step is sound, but B's propagation design is clearer and more robust.
